name: Embedded Systems & IoT
tagline: Program the chips inside everyday devices and connect them to the internet and AI.

overview.summary: Embedded engineers write software that runs directly on hardware — microcontrollers and processors inside phones, cars, medical devices, smart meters, wearables and factory machines. IoT (Internet of Things) engineers connect those devices to networks and the cloud so they can be monitored and controlled remotely. The field also includes chip design and verification (VLSI). A fast-growing area is edge AI: running machine-learning models directly on small devices for privacy, speed and low power.
whyTrending: Global investment in semiconductors and electronics manufacturing (driven by AI chips, EVs and supply-chain diversification) increases demand for embedded and chip engineers.
Edge AI lets devices run models locally — cameras, wearables and industrial sensors increasingly need engineers who can deploy ML on constrained hardware.
BLS reports a 2025 US median of $161,740 for computer hardware engineers, one of the highest-paid engineering occupations, with 9% projected growth (2025–35).

Bangladesh has a growing chip-design and electronics sector — semiconductor design-services firms in Dhaka and local electronics manufacturers — creating niche but well-paid opportunities, with IC Design Engineers among the higher Paylab salary bands.

roles.title: Embedded Software Engineer
roles.description: Writes firmware in C/C++ for microcontrollers: drivers, real-time tasks, power management and communication protocols.

roles.title: IoT Engineer
roles.description: Builds connected-device systems: device firmware, wireless connectivity, cloud ingestion and dashboards.

roles.title: Embedded Linux Engineer
roles.description: Customises Linux for devices (Yocto, Buildroot), writes kernel drivers and manages updates.

roles.title: ASIC / FPGA Design & Verification Engineer
roles.description: Designs and verifies digital chips and FPGA logic using Verilog/SystemVerilog and UVM.

roles.title: Edge AI Engineer
roles.description: Optimises and deploys ML models on microcontrollers, NPUs and edge devices.

roles.title: Firmware Test / Validation Engineer
roles.description: Builds hardware-in-the-loop tests and validates devices against specifications and standards.

beginner: C programming: pointers, memory, bit manipulation
Digital electronics: logic, voltage, current, resistors, transistors
Microcontroller basics with Arduino or ESP32
Using a multimeter and basic soldering
intermediate: Communication protocols: UART, I2C, SPI, CAN
RTOS concepts with FreeRTOS or Zephyr
Wireless: Wi-Fi, BLE, LoRa, cellular IoT
Debugging with JTAG/SWD, logic analysers and oscilloscopes
advanced: Embedded Linux, device trees and kernel drivers
Secure boot, firmware signing and over-the-air updates
Edge AI with TensorFlow Lite Micro / LiteRT, Edge Impulse

tools: AWS IoT Core / Azure IoT Hub
stack.note: C is required in almost every embedded listing; C++ and Python are close behind. Rust is appearing in security-sensitive firmware roles. Chip-design roles focus on SystemVerilog, UVM and EDA tools.

roadmap.title: C and microcontrollers
goals: Strengthen C: pointers, structs, bit operations, memory layout
Get an Arduino or ESP32 board and blink an LED
Read sensors (temperature, light, motion) and print values
Read one full datasheet section for a sensor you use
roadmap.milestone: A sensor-reading device that logs data reliably using interrupts.

roadmap.title: Protocols, RTOS and connectivity
goals: Communicate with sensors over I2C and SPI
Move to an STM32 or ESP-IDF project in plain C (no Arduino layer)
Use FreeRTOS tasks, queues and semaphores
Send sensor data to the cloud over MQTT
roadmap.milestone: A connected IoT device sending data to a live dashboard.

roadmap.title: Production-grade and edge AI
goals: Add low-power sleep modes and measure battery life
Deploy a small ML model (e.g. keyword spotting) with Edge Impulse or LiteRT Micro
Write unit tests for firmware logic
Document the hardware, firmware architecture and test results
roadmap.milestone: A low-power IoT device with OTA updates and an on-device ML feature.

interview.question: What does the 'volatile' keyword do in C?
interview.answer: It tells the compiler a variable may change outside the program's control (hardware registers, ISRs), so it must not optimise away reads/writes.

interview.question: What is an interrupt and an ISR?
interview.answer: An interrupt is a hardware/software signal that pauses normal execution; the Interrupt Service Routine handles it. ISRs should be short and defer heavy work.

interview.question: I2C vs SPI vs UART?
interview.answer: UART is simple asynchronous point-to-point serial. I2C uses two wires and addresses for many devices at moderate speed. SPI uses more wires but is faster and full-duplex.

interview.question: What is an RTOS and when do you need one?
interview.answer: A real-time operating system schedules tasks with predictable timing. Use it when you have multiple concurrent tasks with deadlines; simple devices can use a super-loop.

interview.question: What is a race condition and how do you prevent it in firmware?
interview.answer: When shared data is accessed concurrently and the result depends on timing. Prevent it with critical sections, disabling interrupts briefly, mutexes or atomic operations.

interview.question: Stack vs heap in embedded systems?
interview.answer: The stack holds local variables and call frames; the heap holds dynamic allocations. Many embedded systems avoid heap allocation to prevent fragmentation and unpredictable timing.

interview.question: How do you reduce power consumption?
interview.answer: Use sleep modes, lower clock speeds, turn off unused peripherals, use interrupts instead of polling, and batch radio transmissions.

interview.question: What is a watchdog timer?
interview.answer: A hardware timer that resets the system if software stops 'kicking' it, recovering from hangs.

interview.question: How would you debug a device that randomly resets?
interview.answer: Check reset-cause registers, power supply stability, watchdog, stack overflow, hard-fault handlers and logs; reproduce under controlled conditions.

interview.question: What is MQTT?
interview.answer: A lightweight publish–subscribe messaging protocol for IoT. Devices publish to topics on a broker, and subscribers receive messages, with QoS levels for reliability.

demandNotes.bangladesh: Moderate and specialised: electronics manufacturers, semiconductor design-services firms, telecom and IoT start-ups hire EEE/CSE graduates with strong C and hardware skills.
demandNotes.remote: Moderate. Firmware and IoT-cloud contracts exist; chip verification is often done at offshore design centres.
demandNotes.global: High. Semiconductor investment, EVs, medical devices and edge AI keep embedded engineers in demand.
